sections.h2: Selling in Brownsville at a glance
sections.html:
Brownsville is the Cameron County seat, at the southern tip of Texas across the Rio Grande from Matamoros. A seller here deals with the Cameron Appraisal District, the county clerk and the county tax office. The mid-2025 population estimate is 192,957, up 3.6% from the 2020 estimates base. Owners occupy 61.7% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $139,900, and renters pay about $923 a month at the median.

About 83.6% of residents age five and older speak another language at home, so it often helps to have contracts and disclosures explained in both languages before anyone signs.

sections.h2: How Cameron CAD sets your value
sections.html:
The Cameron Appraisal District sets the value, and each taxing unit picks its own rate. The district's FAQ says every property is reappraised at least once in three years, and yearly where the market moves fast.

No notice of appraised value is required when the value rises by $1,000 or less, so some owners never get a mailing. Under Section 23.23 of the Tax Code, in force since January 1, 2008, a homestead's assessed value can climb only 10% a year. Added rooms, pools and similar improvements fall outside that cap.

Every applicant must show Texas residency, such as a driver's license, and both spouses must apply and supply identification. The exemptions for a primary residence are homestead, over-65, disabled person and 100% disabled veteran. A disabled veteran exemption can instead go on any one property the veteran owns.

  • You can claim over-65 or disabled in a given year, not both.
  • If only some co-owners live in the house, the account is split and the exemption is multiplied by the qualifying owner's share of ownership.
  • The school tax ceiling goes up when you add a pool, garage or room, and it can move to a new Texas homestead on a Tax Ceiling Transfer form.

A few exemption types need a new application by April 30 each year. Ask the district which ones apply to you.

A protest has to be in writing. The deadline is whichever comes later, May 15 or 30 days after the notice was delivered. You can mail it, hand it in or email it, and a mailed filing needs a postmark on or before the cutoff.

After the deadline, neither an appraiser nor the review board can change the value. Hospitalization may count as good cause, but forgetting the date does not. A timely protest earns at least 15 days' notice of a hearing, and hearings usually last about 15 minutes. If you disagree with the result you have three choices: district court, binding arbitration, or, in Cameron County, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

  • Identify the owner and the property by address or account number.
  • Say what you are contesting, such as market value.
  • Attach comparable sales, photos or repair estimates.

Value and the tax lien both date to January 1. The Cameron County Tax Office shares an East Levee Street address with the county clerk. Ask that office which taxing units bill your address, and what the payoff is.

Texas property tax dates that apply to a Brownsville seller
DateWhat happens
January 1Value and the year's lien are set
April 30Some exemption types need a new application
May 15 or 30 days after noticeProtest deadline, whichever is later
Around October 1Bills arrive
February 1Unpaid balances turn delinquent, with a six percent penalty plus one percent interest
After July 1Penalty rises to 12 percent; a unit's attorney may add up to 20 percent

Title can't be cleared while delinquent tax is outstanding, so pay any balance at or before closing.

sections.h2: What if the property is headed for a tax sale?
sections.html:
Tax sales are auctions run by constables or hired agents. No statewide list exists, so watch the county tax office and clerk sites for notices.

Owners of a homestead, farm or mineral interest can redeem within two years after the buyer's deed is filed. The price is a 25% premium in year one or 50% in year two, plus costs. Other property has 180 days and a premium up to 25%. A former owner has two years from the sale to claim any surplus proceeds.

Family land in the Valley sometimes stays in the name of someone who died long ago. An affidavit of heirship is sworn and filed with the county clerk, but no court reviews it and no title insurer has to accept it.

Stronger routes include probate within four years, a muniment of title where the only debts are liens on the real estate, or a transfer on death deed filed before the owner's death. For exemption purposes, heirs who aren't on a recorded deed can give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Where a Brownsville deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Cameron County Clerk, at 835 E. Levee Street in Brownsville, keeps deeds, liens, plats and maps. Cameron CAD updates ownership once it receives the recorded instrument or its volume and page numbers.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus further fees. Ask the clerk for the total on your deed.

A cash offer in Brownsville mostly turns on title and taxes. Get the offer in writing, then have the title company pull the tax balance from the county tax office, check for liens, and confirm who has authority to sign. With a loan, add a mortgage payoff figure. With an inherited house, add whichever probate or affidavit route fits. The deed is signed, acknowledged and recorded with the county clerk, and Cameron CAD updates its account afterward. Buyers who plan to live in the house file their own homestead exemption, since yours doesn't carry over.

faqs.q: What does a typical Brownsville home cost?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $139,900. Your own price depends on condition, lot and street.

faqs.q: Will Cameron CAD always mail a value notice?
faqs.a: No. Notices go to those entitled by law, and none is required when value rises by $1,000 or less.

faqs.q: When is a Brownsville appraisal protest due?
faqs.a: On the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice was delivered. File it in writing, by mail, by hand or by email.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my Brownsville deed?
faqs.a: From the Cameron County Clerk's office on East Levee Street. The appraisal district doesn't supply deeds, surveys or plats.

faqs.q: Does a Brownsville homeowner over 65 get a tax ceiling?
faqs.a: Yes. School taxes on the home generally stop rising while you own and live there, and the ceiling can move to a new Texas homestead.
